findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff defines `def self.downsize` twice in the same module body (once taking `max_width, max_height`, then again three lines later taking `dimensions`), so Ruby silently redefines the method and only the second definition exists at runtime. Every existing caller that invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, w, h)` (the two-argument-dimensions calling convention used throughout the codebase for thumbnails/avatars) now has `h` bound to the `opts` parameter and `w` passed alone as `dimensions`, producing malformed geometry strings and broken thumbnails site-wide; the earlier definition is dead code that hides this.

[BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` passes "80%" where the method (after the duplicate-definition overwrite) forwards it as `dimensions` to `downsize_instructions`, which parses geometry as `WxH`. `downsize_instructions` splits/regex-matches "80%" expecting `width x height`, raising NoMethodError/ArgumentError (e.g., nil.to_i comparison) inside the create_upload rescue block, so the upload silently falls through to `Upload.create_for` with the still-oversized tempfile and fails with a generic error instead of downsizing — the entire feature is a no-op that throws.

[ADVISORY] `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` can never take effect because `optimize` gates the animated path on `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, and `tempfile.path` is `discourse-upload-<type>` with no extension. Animated GIF uploads above the size limit skip the animated-preserving instructions and run the static downsize path on every upload of an animated image; operators who enable animated thumbnails get silently flattened/first-frame-only images.

[ADVISORY] The client now hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, decoupling the client-side validation from the server setting. Admins who raise the setting above 10MB get a client-side alert blocking uploads the server would accept; admins who lower it below 10MB rely solely on server-side handling, and the 413 error message also reports a wrong 10MB figure — every operator changing the setting is bitten immediately.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` with `from` and `to` as the same path, but `convert_with` executes the command with output suppressed (`&> /dev/null`) and returns false without raising on failure. If ImageMagick refuses in-place same-file conversion (or fails for any reason), the loop spins all 5 iterations, discards the failure silently, and `Upload.create_for` proceeds with the original oversized tempfile — the user gets the raw size-limit error with no indication downsizing was attempted and failed.

[BUG] The diff adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` while leaving the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in place, so the latter definition silently shadows the former and every existing caller that passes separate width/height arguments now crashes. Any existing call site invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height)` resolves to the new 4-arg signature: `height` is bound to `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Integer into String / TypeError on Symbol#[]), breaking thumbnail generation for posts with images; it also fires a 'method redefined' warning and the deleted `dimensions` helper makes the old intent unreachable.

[BUG] The client-side size check hardcodes `maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024` for every upload type, dropping the per-type `max_${type}_size_kb` site setting that previously governed attachments and other non-image types. For `type === 'attachment'` (and any non-image type), sites with `max_attachment_size_kb` above or below 10240 now enforce the wrong limit: a 5MB attachment on a site allowing 50MB is rejected in the browser even though the server would accept it, and a site capping attachments at 2MB gets up to 10MB pushed to the server where it fails with a generic server error instead of the client-side message.

[BUG] The downsizing loop applies to any upload whose filename looks like an image, including uploads of `type 'attachment'`, and after 5 iterations of '80%' a still-oversized image is passed to `Upload.create_for` anyway. An image that is 10x the limit (e.g. 50MB against a 512KB `max_image_size_kb`) is only reduced to ~16% of original size (0.8^5), still exceeds the setting, and the upload then fails inside `Upload.create_for` with a stale/mismatched error after server CPU was burned running ImageMagick five times; meanwhile image attachments that would have been stored as files get silently recompressed, corrupting the user's original file.

[ADVISORY] The 413 error handler now hardcodes '10 MB' as the reported max size, but the server's actual enforced limit for non-downsized files remains `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (and per-type attachment settings), so the message shown to users is wrong whenever the setting differs from 10240. Users who hit an entity-too-large error from nginx/the server are told the limit is 10MB regardless of the real configured limit, then retry a 9MB file that still fails — a support/confusion cost on any site with a non-default setting.

[ADVISORY] No verification exists anywhere in the diff for the new server-side downsizing behavior; the diff contains no test-shaped files, no spec updates for uploads_controller or optimized_image, and no coverage for the resize loop's termination, the animated-GIF path, or the oversized-after-5-attempts case. The new mutation of the user's original tempfile (destructive, in-place via `tempfile.path, tempfile.path`) ships with zero regression protection — a future change to `downsize`'s signature or the loop condition would silently ship broken image uploads, and the existing behavior 'original bytes are preserved' is intentionally broken with no test asserting the new downsized result is what gets stored.

[ADVISORY] The image check uses only `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` on the client-supplied filename and never inspects the tempfile's actual content type, so a non-image renamed to `.png` skips downsizing while an actual image whose URL/filename lacks an extension (API URL downloads strip to `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)`) skips downsizing too. API-driven uploads of extension-less image URLs exceed the limit and fail with a generic error, defeating the feature for exactly the URL-download path the same method adds (`file.nil? && url.present?`), and the filename-based gate trusts attacker-controlled input for a behavior branch.

[BUG] The client-side size check replaces the per-type site setting with a hardcoded 10MB, allowing all uploads of any type up to 10MB even when the admin's max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb is far lower. A site with max_image_size_kb=500 sees users routinely upload 10MB images (the client no longer blocks them) and every such upload triggers a server-side 5-iteration downsize loop, multiplying CPU/convert load; non-image types (attachments) also bypass the setting entirely, so the feature changes the enforcement contract for uploads that are never downsized.

[BUG] The 413 error path hardcodes 10MB instead of reading SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, so the error message reports a limit that has nothing to do with the server's actual configured limit. When the server rejects an upload with 413 under its real configured limit (e.g. 1MB), the user is told the max is 10MB and retries the same file, hitting 413 again in a loop with misleading guidance.

[BUG] The 413 error path on the server is never updated to match the new client allowance: the controller still lets the web server (nginx/Rails) reject requests above the configured client_max_body_size / max_image_size_kb before the downsize code runs. For any image larger than the server's request-body limit, the 413 fires before create_upload's downsize loop executes, so the advertised feature ("automatically downsize large images") does not work for the very images it targets; only the SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb check inside Upload.create_for is bypassed, not the HTTP-layer limit.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called in-place with from == to (tempfile.path twice) while the animation branch (GIF + allow_animated) routes to downsize_instructions_animated which builds commands expecting distinct input/output paths, and with '80%' as dimensions the animated-instruction geometry parsing is undefined behavior. Uploading a large GIF with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled runs convert on the same file as both source and destination with percent geometry, producing a corrupted or zero-byte image that is then stored via Upload.create_for.

[BUG] The downsize loop runs a fixed 5 iterations with '80%' each time (0.8^5 ≈ 0.33 linear scale, and much smaller than 33% on file size), with no check of whether conversion actually succeeded or reduced size, and never verifies the final size before Upload.create_for re-checks it. A 30MB JPEG with max_image_size_kb set to, say, 10MB still exceeds the limit after 5 passes and Upload.create_for fails with an unexplained 'file too large' error after the user waited through 5 sequential ImageMagick invocations; also if convert fails the loop silently burns 5 attempts on the same unmodified file.

[BUG] The image check uses FileHelper.is_image?(filename) where filename is derived from the user-supplied name (and from the URL path for API uploads), not from the tempfile's detected content type, while the setting it guards (max_image_size_kb) applies to content-type images. An upload with a .txt or extensionless filename containing image content is silently skipped by the downsize loop and rejected by Upload.create_for's size check, so the automatic-downsize feature fails for images whose name lacks a recognizable image extension.

[BUG] def self.downsize is defined twice in the same module (lines for the width/height variant and the dimensions-string variant), and the second definition silently overwrites the first, breaking all existing callers that pass (from, to, max_width, max_height, opts). Every existing call site of OptimizedImage.downsize with four coordinate arguments (e.g. thumbnail/optimized-image generation paths elsewhere in the codebase) now has its max_width interpreted as a raw geometry string like '150' — ImageMagick treats '150' as a width, not a max-width — and the max_height argument lands in the opts hash, silently producing wrongly resized images across all thumbnail generation.

[ADVISORY] The download-from-URL branch for API uploads hardcodes 10.megabytes, replacing SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, duplicating the same magic constant already hardcoded twice in the client utilities.js — three copies of '10MB' with no single source of truth. The next person tuning this limit must find and update three sites in two languages; the client and server constants will drift, and the actual enforceable limit is still the un-updated server body-size limits.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop mutates the user's uploaded tempfile in place, so the original uploaded bytes are destroyed and the sha1/fingerprint recorded by Upload.create_for describes the altered file, not what the user uploaded. Operators auditing uploads (or dedup logic matching on file hash) get hashes of server-mutated files, and there is no retained original, making later re-optimization or forensic inspection of the true upload impossible.

[BUG] The new 4-argument `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined directly below the (from, to, max_width, max_height) version in the same class body, so the second definition silently shadows the first, and every existing caller passing width and height now binds max_width into `dimensions` and max_height into `opts`. All pre-existing OptimizedImage.downsize call sites (thumbnail generation, avatar resizing) that call downsize(path, path, width, height) hit the new signature: an Integer width is passed as the dimensions string and the Integer height is passed as opts, so downsize_instructions receives garbage geometry and opts[:allow_animation] is nil — every image optimization after this diff produces wrong output or a failed convert, corrupting thumbnails site-wide.

[BUG] The client-side size check replaces the per-type SiteSetting lookup (`max_image_size_kb` / `max_attachment_size_kb`) with a hardcoded 10 * 1024, so the client no longer enforces the admin-configured limit for any upload type. On sites where max_attachment_size_kb (or max_image_size_kb) is set below or above 10MB, the client validates against 10MB while the server still enforces the SiteSetting — attachments larger than the server's configured limit pass the client check and then fail server-side with a generic 413, and admins who raise/lower the setting see no effect on the client gate.

[ADVISORY] The 413 handler hardcodes the reported max size as 10MB instead of the server's actual configured limit. Users on a site whose server limit differs from 10MB get an error message quoting a number the server is not actually enforcing, sending them on a futile loop of re-compressing to meet a phantom limit.

[ADVISORY] The downsize loop passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`, but `OptimizedImage.optimize` only takes the animated code path when `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`, and `tempfile.path` is a Rails tempfile whose path never ends in .gif — the extension lives only in `filename`. The allow_animation option is dead on this path: animated GIF uploads never get animated-aware instructions, so the animated decision is made from the wrong file name and animated thumbnails behave inconsistently between this path and the normal optimized-image path.

[ADVISORY] The fixed 5-iteration loop shrinking by "80%" geometry is a magic-number convergence scheme with no check of convert's exit status and no guarantee of reaching the target: 0.8^5 scaling leaves ~33% of the linear dimensions (≈10% of the pixel area), so a large image against a small max_image_size_kb still exceeds the limit after 5 attempts. Users uploading near-10MB images to sites with small max_image_size_kb settings burn up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick subprocess spawns per upload request on the web hot path and then still get the file-too-large rejection — slow request, wasted CPU, and no feedback that the auto-downsize was attempted but failed; the failure mode is invisible because the loop never inspects convert's return value.

[BUG] The client-side upload check silently replaces the admin-configurable SiteSetting max size with a hardcoded 10MB, changing the enforceable contract of the feature without any acceptance of that change. Operators who set max_image_size_kb above 10MB get client-side rejections the server would accept (users see a wrong 'file too large' error), and operators who set it below 10MB see users pass the client gate only to be downsized server-side — the PR's stated intent was 'automatically downsize large images', not 'remove admin control over client-side size validation', so this is objective drift smuggled in alongside the feature.

[BUG] The 413 error handler also hardcodes 10MB, so the error message shown to users no longer reflects the server's actual configured limit. On a server with max_image_size_kb = 2048, a user whose upload is rejected with 413 is told the limit is 10240KB, a wrong statement of the policy that governs them.

[BUG] The diff defines self.downsize twice, so the first definition (from, to, max_width, max_height) is silently discarded and every existing caller invoking downsize(from, to, width, height) now raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 4 for 3). Any out-of-diff call site using the original four-argument downsize signature — the signature the diff itself still declares at lines 144-146 — crashes at runtime instead of resizing, a silent public-surface break hidden by Ruby's duplicate-method-definition semantics.

[BUG] downsize is called with the literal string "80%" as its dimensions argument, but optimize passes that string to downsize_instructions which was designed to receive a WxH dimensions string built by the now-deleted dimensions() helper. The generated ImageMagick command receives a malformed geometry (e.g. embedded into a WxH template or passed where a pixel geometry is required), so the downsizing loop either fails on every iteration — leaving the file unchanged and Upload.create_for rejecting it with the original size error the feature was meant to eliminate — or produces corrupted output written in-place to tempfile.path.

[ADVISORY] The API/URL download path hardcodes 10.megabytes, replacing SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb as the download cap, which silently removes the operator's configured limit for API uploads specifically. Admins who lower max_image_size_kb cannot bound API-URL downloads below 10MB, and those who raise it above 10MB have API downloads truncated where direct uploads succeed — a behavioral asymmetry between the two upload paths introduced without any stated requirement.

[ADVISORY] The new downsizing block runs for every image upload attempt without any feature flag or SiteSetting gate (beyond max_image_size_kb > 0), and mutates the user's tempfile in place before Upload.create_for records it, so the stored upload is a server-modified image that was never shown or consented to by the uploader. Users uploading a large image get a silently re-encoded (quality-loss) file stored and served; combined with the 5-attempt cap, files that still exceed the limit after five 80% passes proceed to Upload.create_for and fail with a size error, after having already spent five synchronous ImageMagick invocations on the request path.

[BUG] The diff removes all server-side enforcement of the upload size limit for images: any size is accepted and merely downsized, so the max_image_size_kb setting no longer rejects anything. An authenticated user uploads a multi-gigabyte 'image' (extension check only, is_image? uses filename) via multipart; the request body is fully buffered to a tempfile before any size check, and ImageMagick then runs up to 5 passes over attacker-controlled bytes — disk-fill and CPU exhaustion DoS on every worker, since the previous behavior (create_for rejecting oversize files / FileHelper.download's byte cap) is bypassed for the normal upload path which never had a pre-save cap other than the site setting.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination, and the loop re-invokes it while tempfile.size is still over the limit — ImageMagick convert with identical input/output paths truncates the output mid-write. The tempfile becomes a corrupt or zero-byte file; the loop can spin all 5 attempts on an empty file (size never drops below limit), and the corrupted bytes are then passed to Upload.create_for and stored as the user's upload — attacker gets to serve arbitrary/truncated image data or a 0-byte upload recorded as valid.

[BUG] The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently shadows the first (width, height) definition, so every existing caller invoking downsize with separate width/height args now has its height argument interpreted as opts and opts dropped. Existing thumbnail-generation call sites pass e.g. downsize(from, to, 100, 200) — the height 200 lands in the opts hash, dimensions becomes '100x' or geometry built from the wrong values, and opts like allow_animation are ignored everywhere, producing wrong thumbnails and skipping animation guards for all other code paths in the app.

[BUG] The downsize loop overwrites the user's original uploaded image file in place before Upload.create_for, silently and irreversibly destroying the original-resolution data with no backup of the pre-resize bytes. The stored upload (and the original full-size image users get when clicking a lightbox) is a re-encoded, progressively-shrunk JPEG/PNG instead of what was uploaded; once saved, the original pixels cannot be recovered, and animated GIFs re-encoded with allow_animation: false lose their animation entirely even when the original was under a different intended use.

[BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in the same module, and the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height), breaking every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments. Any call site outside this diff that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) now binds the Integer height into opts, so opts[:allow_animation] inside optimize raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) and thumbnail generation crashes instead of producing a resized image.

[BUG] The loop bails out after 5 attempts even if tempfile.size is still above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized file and no guarantee of error handling distinct from the pre-feature path. Images that resist 5 rounds of 80% downscaling (e.g., already small dimensions with high entropy, or allow_animated_thumbnails keeping animated frames) are passed to Upload.create_for oversized; the upload either fails validation after the original file was already destroyed by the in-place downsize, or is stored in violation of the size limit.

[BUG] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failed ImageMagick convert is silently retried and then the oversize/corrupted file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. When convert_with fails (exitstatus != 0), it returns false with no exception and no log; the loop re-reads tempfile.size, retries 5 times, then falls through and uploads the original oversized file — and because downsize operates in-place (from == to), a partially-written failed convert can leave the tempfile corrupted, so the user's image is destroyed and replaced by an opaque generic upload error with nothing logged server-side.

[BUG] Defining self.downsize a second time in the same module silently overrides the first definition, so the width/height-arity variant no longer exists and its callers crash. Any existing call site invoking downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height) now resolves to the dimensions-string version with max_height bound to opts (an Integer), and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) — every such thumbnail-generation call 500s. Ruby has no method overloading; the first def is dead code that hides this.

[ADVISORY] The 80%-per-iteration, 5-iteration downsize loop cannot converge for sufficiently large inputs, and the overflow path is a silent partial success of the auto-downsize feature. Five passes of 80% linear dimensions reduce file size at most to roughly 10% of original (area ~0.64^5), so e.g. a 100MB photo ends near but often still above a 10MB limit; the loop exits without any error or log and the still-oversized file goes to Upload.create_for, where the user gets a plain file_too_large error despite the feature promising automatic reduction — no signal distinguishes 'downsize mathematically insufficient' from 'downsize worked'.

[ADVISORY] The client-side size cap is hardcoded to 10MB, decoupling it from the server's SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb in both directions. An admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB has valid uploads rejected in the browser with a 'file too large' dialog naming a limit the server doesn't enforce; one who lowers it below 10MB gets no client hint and relies solely on the server error — the two enforcement points drift with no single source of truth.

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a duplicate `self.downsize` definition in `optimized_image.rb` (the later one overwrites the earlier 4-arg version) and `UploadsController` now calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)`. However, the finding’s key claim—that `downsize_instructions` parses `dimensions` strictly as `WxH` and will raise (e.g., via split/regex leading to nil/to_i errors)—cannot be verified from the shown diff because the implementation of `downsize_instructions` is not included. From the diff alone, `dimensions` is simply forwarded to `*_instructions`, and `"80%"` could be a valid geometry string depending on how instructions are constructed. Therefore the asserted runtime exception/no-op behavior is not demonstrably grounded in the provided changes.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `optimized_image.rb`, the animated code path is selected only when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true **and** `from =~ /\.GIF$/i`. But `from` here is `tempfile.path`, and for the URL-download case the tempfile is created with a basename like `"discourse-upload-#{type}"` (no `.gif` extension shown in the diff). Therefore, even for animated GIF uploads, the regex gate can fail and the non-animated instructions are used, potentially flattening/losing animation despite `allow_animated_thumbnails` being enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new downsizing block runs for every image upload attempt without any feature flag or SiteSetting gate (beyond max_image_size_kb > 0), and mutates the user's tempfile in place before Upload.create_for records it, so the stored upload is a server-modified image that was never shown or consented to by the uploader. Users uploading a large image get a silently re-encoded (quality-loss) file stored and served; combined with the 5-attempt cap, files that still exceed the limit after five 80% passes proceed to Upload.create_for and fail with a size error, after having already spent five synchronous ImageMagick invocations on the request path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional (for images) downsizing loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` guarded only by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0` and `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)`, and it overwrites `tempfile.path` in place via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` before `Upload.create_for` runs. This means the stored upload can be silently re-encoded/quality-reduced without any explicit user-facing acknowledgement or a dedicated feature flag. Also, the loop is capped at 5 attempts and then continues to `Upload.create_for` even if still oversized, so the request may spend up to five ImageMagick conversions and still fail size validation. These are concrete, diff-grounded product/performance concerns, but not a clearly verifiable functional defect given the comment indicating this behavior is intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes all server-side enforcement of the upload size limit for images: any size is accepted and merely downsized, so the max_image_size_kb setting no longer rejects anything. An authenticated user uploads a multi-gigabyte 'image' (extension check only, is_image? uses filename) via multipart; the request body is fully buffered to a tempfile before any size check, and ImageMagick then runs up to 5 passes over attacker-controlled bytes — disk-fill and CPU exhaustion DoS on every worker, since the previous behavior (create_for rejecting oversize files / FileHelper.download's byte cap) is bypassed for the normal upload path which never had a pre-save cap other than the site setting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not remove server-side size enforcement entirely. In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the new downsizing loop runs *before* `Upload.create_for(...)`, but the code still passes `tempfile.size` into `create_for`, so any size validation inside `Upload.create_for` is still in play (not shown as removed here). Also, the URL-download path still has an explicit cap, changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes`, so it’s not “any size accepted”. The claim about multi-gigabyte multipart buffering and bypassing all limits cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is called with tempfile.path as both source and destination, and the loop re-invokes it while tempfile.size is still over the limit — ImageMagick convert with identical input/output paths truncates the output mid-write. The tempfile becomes a corrupt or zero-byte file; the loop can spin all 5 attempts on an empty file (size never drops below limit), and the corrupted bytes are then passed to Upload.create_for and stored as the user's upload — attacker gets to serve arbitrary/truncated image data or a 0-byte upload recorded as valid.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` using the same path as both input and output inside a retry loop. From the diff, `OptimizedImage.optimize` ultimately shells out to an ImageMagick command via `convert_with(instructions, to)` without any safeguard against in-place conversion, and the controller ignores the return value (failure/success). This can plausibly corrupt/truncate the tempfile or otherwise produce an invalid file while still proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)` with whatever bytes are on disk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently shadows the first (width, height) definition, so every existing caller invoking downsize with separate width/height args now has its height argument interpreted as opts and opts dropped. Existing thumbnail-generation call sites pass e.g. downsize(from, to, 100, 200) — the height 200 lands in the opts hash, dimensions becomes '100x' or geometry built from the wrong values, and opts like allow_animation are ignored everywhere, producing wrong thumbnails and skipping animation guards for all other code paths in the app.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, there are two `def self.downsize` definitions after the change: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and later one taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby, the later definition overrides the earlier one, so the 4-argument (width/height) API is silently removed. Any existing callers using the old signature would now have their arguments mis-bound (e.g., height treated as `opts`) and lose options like `allow_animation`. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable defect (method shadowing / breaking API).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop overwrites the user's original uploaded image file in place before Upload.create_for, silently and irreversibly destroying the original-resolution data with no backup of the pre-resize bytes. The stored upload (and the original full-size image users get when clicking a lightbox) is a re-encoded, progressively-shrunk JPEG/PNG instead of what was uploaded; once saved, the original pixels cannot be recovered, and animated GIFs re-encoded with allow_animation: false lose their animation entirely even when the original was under a different intended use.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`, using the same path for input and output. That overwrites the uploaded tempfile in place before `Upload.create_for(...)` reads it, so the stored upload is the downsized/re-encoded result rather than the original bytes. This is irreversible data loss relative to the original upload and can also drop GIF animation when `allow_animation` is false (since `optimize` selects non-animated instructions unless `opts[:allow_animation]` is truthy).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedImage.downsize is defined twice in the same module, and the second definition (from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the first (from, to, max_width, max_height), breaking every existing caller that passes width and height as separate arguments. Any call site outside this diff that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) now binds the Integer height into opts, so opts[:allow_animation] inside optimize raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) and thumbnail generation crashes instead of producing a resized image.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff leaves two `self.downsize` method definitions: one taking `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and later another taking `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the later definition overwrites the former, so any existing caller still passing width/height as separate args will now call the new signature, binding `height` into `opts` (an Integer). `optimize` then does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise a TypeError on an Integer, breaking image downsizing/thumbnail generation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loop bails out after 5 attempts even if tempfile.size is still above SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the still-oversized file and no guarantee of error handling distinct from the pre-feature path. Images that resist 5 rounds of 80% downscaling (e.g., already small dimensions with high entropy, or allow_animated_thumbnails keeping animated frames) are passed to Upload.create_for oversized; the upload either fails validation after the original file was already destroyed by the in-place downsize, or is stored in violation of the size limit.

adjudication.rationale: The new controller logic downsizes in-place up to 5 times (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes ... OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%" ...)`), but after the loop it unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without an explicit post-check/early return if the file is still above `max_image_size_kb`. The diff doesn’t show whether `Upload.create_for` will always enforce the limit, so the claim that it will be stored “in violation” isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the missing explicit handling of the “still too large after attempts” edge case is a concrete issue introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failed ImageMagick convert is silently retried and then the oversize/corrupted file is passed to Upload.create_for anyway. When convert_with fails (exitstatus != 0), it returns false with no exception and no log; the loop re-reads tempfile.size, retries 5 times, then falls through and uploads the original oversized file — and because downsize operates in-place (from == to), a partially-written failed convert can leave the tempfile corrupted, so the user's image is destroyed and replaced by an opaque generic upload error with nothing logged server-side.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` but ignores its return value and has no logging/error handling. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` when ImageMagick exits non-zero and otherwise returns `nil`, so failures are silent (`&> /dev/null`) and the loop will just retry based on `tempfile.size`. After retries, the code unconditionally falls through to `Upload.create_for(...)` without verifying the file is now under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` or that downsizing succeeded, meaning an oversized and/or partially-modified in-place file can be passed onward.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Defining self.downsize a second time in the same module silently overrides the first definition, so the width/height-arity variant no longer exists and its callers crash. Any existing call site invoking downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height) now resolves to the dimensions-string version with max_height bound to opts (an Integer), and `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer raises TypeError (no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) — every such thumbnail-generation call 500s. Ruby has no method overloading; the first def is dead code that hides this.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb, `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is still present but then a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined later in the same class, which in Ruby overrides the earlier method (no overloading). As a result, any existing call site using the 4-arg form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` will bind `max_height` (an Integer) to `opts`, and `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` will fail (Integer `[]` with a Symbol causes TypeError), breaking thumbnail generation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 80%-per-iteration, 5-iteration downsize loop cannot converge for sufficiently large inputs, and the overflow path is a silent partial success of the auto-downsize feature. Five passes of 80% linear dimensions reduce file size at most to roughly 10% of original (area ~0.64^5), so e.g. a 100MB photo ends near but often still above a 10MB limit; the loop exits without any error or log and the still-oversized file goes to Upload.create_for, where the user gets a plain file_too_large error despite the feature promising automatic reduction — no signal distinguishes 'downsize mathematically insufficient' from 'downsize worked'.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new auto-downsize block loops up to 5 times calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", ...)` but then unconditionally proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` without checking whether the file is now <= `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. If the downsize attempts don’t bring the file under the limit, the user will still hit the normal oversize rejection path with no specific signal that auto-downsize was attempted/insufficient. The finding’s UX/edge-case concern is grounded in the diff, though the exact “10%” bound is an approximation rather than strictly verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The client-side size cap is hardcoded to 10MB, decoupling it from the server's SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb in both directions. An admin who raises max_image_size_kb above 10MB has valid uploads rejected in the browser with a 'file too large' dialog naming a limit the server doesn't enforce; one who lowers it below 10MB gets no client hint and relies solely on the server error — the two enforcement points drift with no single source of truth.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hardcodes the client-side max size to 10MB in `utilities.js` (both the initial file size check and the 413 handler), replacing `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` / `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb`. This means browser enforcement and the displayed limit can diverge from server-side `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (still referenced in `uploads_controller.rb` for downsizing/limits), so admins raising the setting above 10MB will see valid uploads rejected client-side, and lowering it below 10MB removes the client hint and relies on server rejection.
